title: Close-area safety-filter kill test A: no filter, PX4 Collision Prevention style and PX4-CBF as shipped on A* under VIO faults, with map-only obstacles the range fan cannot see
summary: Harness that puts a safety filter between a planner and the vehicle in the shared close-area-arena, for the kill test of the hub's integrity-aware safety-filter headline. filters.py defines the SafetyFilter interface filter(setpoint, pose, scan, map_obstacles, health, dt) -> (setpoint, intervened), a registry, and three arms: F0 pass-through; F1 CP-stop, PX4 Collision Prevention style per-sector velocity limit with CP_DIST, CP_DELAY, jerk-limited braking, sliding and CP_GUIDE_ANG guidance (read from PX4 docs; CP_DIST 0.5 m is ours); F2 PX4-CBF as shipped in the NTNU fork, the analytic single-constraint composite CBF on body-frame range points with doc 05 Table II gains, linear class-K, raw input, clamp after, low-passed output and no FoV constraint, wrapped around the planner's velocity setpoint with a P velocity loop. unsensed.py adds two map-only obstacles per layout (thin poles or glass panels) on the reference A* path: they are in the prior grid and truth collision checks but a wrapped range fan cannot see them. run_kill.py runs astar_esdf(known_map=True) on 100 random layouts under the arena estimator's none, jump, bias and dropout faults plus a truth reference, for each arm, with the unsensed obstacles on and off, and scores on truth. numpy + scipy only.
verified: ran 2026-11-09 with CPython 3.11.15 + numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1 on an Apple M3 Max, in the sample venv: run_kill.py --layouts 100 --seed 0 --workers 14 ran 3000 runs in 176.4 s and wrote results/kill_a_*; a rerun of 24 of those runs in one process gave identical scores. With F0, truth pose and unsensed obstacles off, the harness reproduced the arena's run.evaluate for astar_esdf exactly on layouts 0-4. Every number in README is from results/. test_smoke.py: 1 passed in the venv, 1 skipped under plain python3 3.14 without numpy. No arena file was edited. Layouts, vehicle, range fan and estimator faults are simulated; no SITL, no PX4 code was run (F1 is a reading of the PX4 docs, F2 follows doc 05's pseudo-code). Later parts (driver-landed, same host and venv): part b (F3 Belief-CBF, F4 MR-CBF sweep, seed 0, 807 s), the integrity monitor (run_monitor.py, 55 s), part d (F5 ours, seed 0, 2800 runs, 194.5 s) and part e (held-out seeds 1-2 and u_trap / narrow_gap seed 1, no parameter changed, 137.8-168.0 s each; Wilson intervals from results/kill_e_tables.py). Parts b, d and the monitor README sections were written by the loop driver from the result files after job time-outs.
shows: Whether a range-only safety filter (PX4 Collision Prevention style, PX4-CBF) already prevents A* collisions under VIO jump, bias and dropout faults, with and without map-only obstacles the range fan cannot see
key_result: [Held-out verdict, Part e](README.md#part-e-held-out-seeds-and-families-ran-2026-11-09-synthetic): the integrity-aware filter (F5, PL margin + hover on ambiguity) FAILS doc 04's kill test on held-out random seeds 1-2: jump collisions 2.5 % [1.1, 5.7] (95 % Wilson, 200 runs) and 0.55 of PX4-CBF's jump reach, while MR-CBF with a fixed 0.2 m bound tuned on seed 0 stays at 1.0 % [0.3, 2.9] or less in every case on seeds 0-2 (pooled 0.33 % vs F5 0.28 %); every F4/F5 collision is a jump run into an unsensed obstacle. Supporting result kept: with every obstacle visible, PX4-CBF has 0 % collisions in every VIO fault case (A* alone 7 % under a jump). Synthetic, A* known map only
